This page corresponds to the exact occupation U.S. O*NET/SOC 25-1071.00 "Health Specialties Teachers, Postsecondary" (Health Specialties Teachers, Postsecondary): teach courses in health specialties, covering fields such as dentistry, laboratory technology, medicine, pharmacy, public health, therapy, and veterinary medicine. Official scope text: Teach courses in health specialties, in fields such as dentistry, laboratory technology, medicine, pharmacy, public health, therapy, and veterinary medicine. The core tasks listed by O*NET include: preparing course materials (such as syllabi, assignments, and handouts; importance 84); following developments in the field by reading current literature, talking with colleagues, and participating in professional conferences (83); evaluating and grading students' class work and assignments and papers (81); supervising laboratory sessions (80); compiling, administering, and grading examinations, or assigning that work to others (79); maintaining student attendance and grade and other necessary records (79); initiating, facilitating, and moderating classroom discussions (78); planning, evaluating, and revising curricula and course content and materials and teaching methods (75); supervising undergraduate or graduate teaching and internship and research work (74); participating in admissions and registration and job placement activities (72); selecting and obtaining materials and supplies such as textbooks and laboratory equipment (70); collaborating with colleagues on teaching and research issues (68); serving on academic or administrative committees dealing with institutional policy and departmental and academic affairs (68); advising students on academic and career curricula and career issues (68); keeping regular office hours to advise and assist students (67); conducting research in a particular field of knowledge and publishing findings in professional journals, books, or electronic media (64); participating in campus and community activities (51); preparing and delivering topics such as public health and stress management and workplace health promotion for undergraduate or graduate students (79); performing administrative duties (such as serving as department head; 77); writing grant proposals to obtain external research funding (69); serving as an adviser to student organizations (60); and compiling specialized bibliographies of materials for outside reading assignments (56). Common job titles include Assistant Professor and Associate Professor and Clinical Professor and Instructor and Lecturer and Occupational Therapy Professor and Pharmacology Professor and Physical Therapy Professor and Professor and Public Health Professor. Scope note: the wage and employment and industry data presented by O*NET on the 25-1071.00 page are not marked as taken from a parent occupation, so this page labels them faithfully according to this occupation's own scope (25-1071.00); the wages on that page show only the annual wage distribution (no hourly wage), and this page does not fill in an hourly wage; the page also shows a projected 2024—2034 growth of "Much faster than average (7% or higher)" (much faster than average) and marks it Bright Outlook (good prospects). Exercise prompt | A completely fictional higher education health specialties course design and teaching task package (for practice workflow only; it does not represent any real institution, program, student, or data). Write a draft plan: (1) how, based on a fictional program of study along with a course syllabus and prerequisites, to arrange a health specialties course in a structured way (program objectives and learning outcomes, course content and sequence and basis, teaching and laboratory and clinical or internship arrangements, assessment and grading and feedback, academic integrity and teaching ethics and safety, evaluation and improvement, and records and files), and state which information is insufficient and needs to be supplemented (prerequisites and academic background, professional and industry standards and accreditation requirements, laboratory or clinical site and safety requirements, assessment and grading definitions and fairness, accessibility and language requirements, and academic integrity and data and privacy requirements); (2) how to design the completion and review points for a fictional teaching, assessment, and grade record table (fields and definitions, students and courses and classes, grades and grading basis and review, exceptions and appeals and corrections, and original records and revision audit trails); (3) how to write a handover-ready course description (program objectives—content and basis—teaching and assessment—ethics and safety—evaluation and improvement—open items); (4) how to record and preserve student grades and teaching files and research data, and distinguish disclosable information from controlled materials or materials involving students' and participants' personal information; (5) how to pause, review, and escalate when academic or academic integrity problems or laboratory or clinical safety risks are found, when privacy or ethics issues are involved, or when the task exceeds the position's authorization. Answer using public materials and simulated data; do not use any real student or participant data.

If you are willing to keep learning in the health specialties field and explain knowledge clearly, can collaborate with students and colleagues and the industry, and are willing to take responsibility for teaching quality and academic integrity and the safety of students, colleagues, and patients, the daily requirements of this occupation are closer to the way you work.

Caution signals | O*NET also shows (25-1071.00, work activity importance scope and work context percentage response scope): Training and Teaching Others (89), Updating and Using Relevant Knowledge (89), Getting Information (87), Working with Computers (86), and Thinking Creatively (83) are the highest activities; contact with others 76%, public speaking 35% every day and 53% once a week or more, time pressure 46% once a week or more, consequence of error 47% very serious, responsibility for others' work outcomes 33% very high and 33% high, responsibility for others' health and safety 42% very high, dealing with unpleasant or angry or discourteous people 16% every day and 44% once a month or more, conflict situations 36% once a week or more, and work schedule 85% regular but working more than 40 hours per week 46%. This occupation takes health specialties course teaching and student advising and teaching research and research as its subject matter, and a single error in a course or materials or assessment, a single grading or grade record mistake, a single improper handling of academic integrity or research ethics, a single safety or privacy error in laboratory or clinical mentoring, or a single out-of-bounds statement involving clinical diagnosis and treatment and medication can all cause harm to students' studies, risks to the safety of students, colleagues, or patients, and reputation and compliance risk for the institution. O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Five (extensive preparation needed, SVP 8.0 and above); the education section of that page shows 36% master's degree, 25% doctoral degree, and 19% post-doctoral training. If you find it hard to teach and communicate with students and peers over the long term, hard to bear responsibility for teaching quality and the safety of students, colleagues, and patients and the consequences of errors, or unwilling to take responsibility for the truthfulness of academic integrity and data and privacy compliance, you should treat these as real costs that need careful weighing.

Ownership judgment | Real fit comes from whether you can do three things at once on the same teaching and research task: do the profession properly (design and teach and assess health specialties courses based on program objectives and professional and industry standards, cite knowledge consistent with current evidence and standards, and produce usable course and assessment and grade and teaching research records), keep compliance and ethics and boundaries under control (work and keep an audit trail in line with academic integrity and teaching ethics and research ethics and student and patient privacy and data protection requirements; distinguish disclosable information from controlled materials or materials involving students' and participants' personal information and handle them according to policy; and do not overstep by providing clinical diagnosis and treatment and medication advice or substituting for clinical qualifications), and take on definable position responsibility (be accountable for the course design and teaching and assessment and grading and advising and teaching research and records you personally perform, and refer matters beyond authorization or involving clinical judgment and medical advice and major institutional decisions and external disclosure to the appropriate position or institution according to policy). It is recommended to test this with one verifiable experience (completing a course and assessment plan and a grade and record note for a fictional course, or a retrospective review of handling one academic integrity or safety or privacy risk) rather than relying only on the conclusions of an interest questionnaire.

Standards and quality boundaries | This page involves three types of requirements: first, professional and quality, meaning course design and teaching and assessment and grading must be carried out on the basis of program objectives and professional and industry standards, with course and assessment and grade and teaching research and research records kept; second, ethics and privacy and academic integrity, meaning courses and student advising must follow academic integrity and teaching and research ethics, and students' and patients' and participants' personal information must be managed in accordance with institutional and legal requirements, and clinical diagnosis and treatment or medication advice must not be provided beyond boundaries; third, records and information, meaning course and assessment and grade and teaching research and research and funding records must be truthful, complete, and traceable, and materials that are controlled or involve personal information and externally disclosed information must be managed according to approval and the minimum necessary principle. This page provides general guidance only and does not constitute medical, diagnostic, treatment, medication, legal, or education policy advice.

Special note: in the United States this occupation falls under O*NET Job Zone Five (extensive preparation needed, SVP 8.0 and above), and the education section shows 36% master's degree, 25% doctoral degree, and 19% post-doctoral training; in mainland China, positions involving higher education and clinical teaching often have requirements for education and teaching qualifications and professional and technical titles and clinical qualifications, so be sure to confirm the position's specific requirements for education and training and qualifications and continuing education and the handling of student and patient information and position authorization.

Notes on verification points | Positions with similar titles differ greatly in duties and authorization: some focus on teaching and course development, some on research and publication and obtaining funding, some on clinical mentoring and internship supervision, and some on administration and departmental governance; different institutions and jurisdictions also differ in the authorization for clinical advice, grades and degrees, student data, and external disclosure; and the assessment and job security of tenure-track versus non-tenure-track versus part-time versus clinical faculty differ markedly.

01 Actual duties and authorization boundaries of the position | Verify whether the role genuinely involves independent course design and teaching and assessment and student advising and teaching research work, or is mainly teaching assistance and materials organization and item writing and exam proctoring and support; verify the teaching platforms and laboratory or clinical sites and tools and data and literature permissions that may be used, the approval requirements for accessing and handling and disclosing student and patient information and research data, the authority over grades and academic sanctions and course changes and programs of study, and the collaboration and reporting paths with teaching administration and research administration and the ethics committee and clinical departments.

Notes on verification points | This occupation frequently teaches and communicates and collaborates with students and peers and the public, and usually requires training and continuing education related to health specialties and education and teaching, and teaching qualifications or professional qualification requirements.

02 Ethics and academic integrity and privacy requirements | Verify whether the institution requires and provides: academic integrity and examination discipline and grading and grade review requirements; teaching and research ethics and ethics review and informed consent requirements; requirements for accessing and storing and sharing and disclosing students' and patients' and participants' personal information; data protection and information security requirements; laboratory or clinical site safety and protection and exposure handling requirements; conflict of interest and funding and authorship standards; accessibility and language and fairness requirements; and teaching and research and ethics committee review paths. This description does not replace the employer's and the competent authority's requirements for education and training and qualifications and continuing education and professional qualifications, and does not constitute any hiring condition.

Notes on verification points | The interface relationships with teaching administration and research administration and the ethics committee and clinical departments determine the boundaries of courses and grades and research and data and responsibility and disclosure, and must be clarified in advance.

paragraphs: Conclusion | The core difference between this page (O*NET 25-1071.00 Health Specialties Teachers, Postsecondary) and adjacent positions lies in "subject matter, output, and authorization level": this occupation takes health specialties course teaching and student advising and teaching research and research as its subject matter, and its output is courses and teaching materials and assessment and grading and advising and teaching research and research findings records; Postsecondary Nursing Instructors and Teachers (25-1072.00) take nursing course teaching and clinical mentoring as their subject matter; Health Education Specialists (21-1091.00) take population health education and promotion programs as their subject matter; Clinical Nurse Specialists (29-1141.04) take clinical nursing and diagnosis and treatment as their subject matter; Postsecondary Biological Science Teachers (25-1042.00) take biological science course teaching as their subject matter; and Career and Technical Education Teachers, Postsecondary (25-1194.00) take career and technical course teaching as their subject matter. Subject matter, output, and authorization level all differ, and the authority for clinical diagnosis and treatment, medical advice, major institutional decisions, and disclosure cannot be carried over across positions.

Evidence note | The comparison subjects in the table below come from the O*NET occupational classification and public materials, and are intended to help distinguish the work content of adjacent occupations and choose a fit; they do not constitute qualification, hiring, or compensation conclusions, nor do they constitute medical, diagnostic, treatment, medication, legal, or education policy advice. The wages and employment of each occupation must be verified separately under its own SOC scope; this table does not make numerical comparisons, nor does it treat one occupation's wages as a proxy for another's; qualification and ethics and data requirements must be verified according to each jurisdiction and institution. The U.S. wage and employment on this page follow this occupation's (25-1071.00) own scope as presented by O*NET on the 25-1071.00 page (that page does not mark them as taken from a parent occupation and shows projected growth of 7% or higher, and the wages show only annual wages and not the hourly wage), and values from adjacent occupations are not borrowed.

Preface | The following comparison is organized in four columns: "career direction—core work and output—key differences—who it suits better." Health specialties teaching, nursing teaching, health education programs, and clinical nursing are often connected within the same medical school or clinical teaching hospital, but connection does not mean they are interchangeable; when choosing across directions, you should relearn that direction's subject matter and standards and data and authorization and responsibility boundaries.

Key differences: this occupation takes health specialties course teaching and student advising and teaching research and research as its subject matter, and, drawing on disciplinary and professional and teaching knowledge, designs and teaches and assesses within academic integrity and ethics and authorization and produces grades and teaching research conclusions, being responsible for teaching quality and the safety of students and patients and records; the other positions center respectively on nursing course teaching, population health education programs, clinical nursing and diagnosis and treatment, biological science course teaching, or career and technical course teaching, and each usually has more specialized standards and qualifications and subject matter, and none bears primary responsibility for health specialties course teaching and teaching research (though they must collaborate with this occupation and clearly define boundaries).

Better suited to people who are willing to keep learning in the health specialties field and explain knowledge clearly, can collaborate with students and peers and the industry, and are willing to take responsibility for teaching quality and academic integrity and the safety of students, colleagues, and patients.

Core work and output: prepare course materials and teach courses and moderate discussions and supervise laboratories, evaluate and grade assignments and papers and compile and administer and grade examinations, maintain student attendance and grade records, supervise teaching and internships and research and hold office hours and advise, conduct research and publish and apply for funding, and participate in admissions and committees and academic service; the output is courses and teaching materials and assessment and grading and advising and teaching research and research findings records (O*NET/SOC 25-1071.00).
This occupation: Health Specialties Teachers, Postsecondary (O*NET/SOC 25-1071.00, Health Specialties Teachers, Postsecondary)

Key differences: Postsecondary Nursing Instructors and Teachers take nursing course teaching and clinical mentoring as their subject matter, and their output is nursing courses and clinical mentoring and assessment records; this occupation takes health specialties (including dentistry and laboratory technology and medicine and public health and therapy and veterinary medicine, etc.) course teaching and teaching research as its subject matter, and its output is course and assessment and teaching research records; the two are highly adjacent, but the disciplines and professional standards and the scope of clinical mentoring differ (collaboration with Postsecondary Nursing Instructors and Teachers is needed to clarify disciplinary and clinical boundaries).

Better suited to people who are willing to work on nursing course teaching and clinical mentoring; this occupation leans more toward health specialties (multidisciplinary) course teaching and teaching research and research.

Core work and output: teach nursing courses according to nursing program standards and carry out clinical mentoring and assessment and record them; the output is nursing courses and clinical mentoring and assessment records.
Postsecondary Nursing Instructors and Teachers (25-1072.00)

Key differences: Health Education Specialists take the design and implementation and evaluation of population health education and promotion programs as their subject matter, and their output is needs assessments and program plans and evaluation records; this occupation takes higher education health specialties course teaching and student advising and teaching research as its subject matter, and its output is course and assessment and teaching research records, and generally does not bear primary responsibility for designing population-facing health education and promotion programs (though collaboration with Health Education Specialists is needed to connect practice and internships).

Better suited to people who are willing to work on designing and implementing population-facing health education and promotion programs; this occupation leans more toward higher education course teaching and student advising and teaching research.

Core work and output: design and implement and evaluate population health education and promotion programs and materials and keep assessment and service-recipient records; the output is needs assessments and program plans and evaluation records.
Health Education Specialists (21-1091.00)

Key differences: Clinical Nurse Specialists take clinical nursing and diagnosis and treatment and patient care as their subject matter, and their output is clinical nursing and diagnosis and treatment records; this occupation takes higher education health specialties course teaching and teaching research as its subject matter, and its output is course and assessment and teaching research records, and generally does not bear primary responsibility for direct clinical care (though during clinical mentoring they must collaborate with Clinical Nurse Specialists and clarify the boundary between teaching and diagnosis and treatment).

Better suited to people who are willing to work on clinical nursing and diagnosis and treatment and patient care; this occupation leans more toward higher education course teaching and student advising and teaching research.

Core work and output: carry out nursing assessment and diagnosis and treatment and care and health education according to clinical nursing standards and record them; the output is clinical nursing and diagnosis and treatment records.
Clinical Nurse Specialists (29-1141.04)

Key differences: Postsecondary Biological Science Teachers take biological science discipline course teaching and laboratories as their subject matter, and their output is biological science courses and laboratory and assessment records; this occupation takes health specialties (clinical and public health and applied health disciplines) course teaching and teaching research as its subject matter, and its output is health specialties courses and assessment and teaching research records; the two are adjacent in discipline and methods, but the professional and industry standards and clinical or practice requirements differ.

Better suited to people who are willing to work on biological science discipline course teaching and laboratories; this occupation leans more toward health specialties course teaching and teaching research and research.

Core work and output: teach biological science courses and supervise laboratories and assessment and conduct discipline research and keep records; the output is biological science courses and laboratory and assessment records.
Biological Science Teachers, Postsecondary (25-1042.00)

Key differences: Career and Technical Education Teachers take career and technical courses and practical training and professional qualification preparation as their subject matter, and their output is career and technical courses and practical training records; this occupation takes higher education health specialties (undergraduate and graduate level) course teaching and teaching research as its subject matter, and its output is course and assessment and teaching research records; the two differ in teaching level and discipline and qualification objectives.

Better suited to people who are willing to work on career and technical courses and practical training and professional qualification preparation; this occupation leans more toward higher education health specialties course teaching and teaching research and research.

Core work and output: teach career and technical courses and organize practical training and professional qualification preparation and assessment and keep records; the output is career and technical courses and practical training records.
Career/Technical Education Teachers, Postsecondary (25-1194.00)

Transition | This page places adjacent positions side by side by "subject matter, output, and authorization level" to help you judge which kind of health specialties teaching or nursing teaching or health education program or clinical nursing or biological science teaching or career and technical teaching position you want to invest in long term. Whichever direction you choose, what really determines whether you can take the job is that direction's subject matter and standards and data and qualification requirements, the ability to write courses and assessments or programs and records clearly, and the willingness to take responsibility for academic integrity and the safety of students, colleagues, and patients; the interest questionnaire is only used to raise questions.

What kind of personality is better suited to being a Health Specialties Teacher, Postsecondary? This occupation values teaching and communication skills, rigor about the discipline and evidence, a sense of responsibility for academic integrity and the safety of students and patients, and stability under semester and research pressure, rather than any particular personality type; the O*NET interest code is SI (Social—Investigative), which can serve as a starting point for exploration.

Are introverts suited to this occupation? Yes. This occupation involves a great deal of lesson preparation and teaching research and writing, and it also requires communicating with the classroom and students (contact with others 76%, public speaking 35% every day and 53% once a week or more).

Introversion and extraversion are not a validated fit threshold here; you can observe teaching, listening to feedback, explaining the grading basis, and confirming understanding. No occupational-level comparative validity research was obtained.

Which MBTI type is most suitable for this occupation? No type has been proven most suitable. The MBTI is not an occupational qualification or ability assessment tool, and occupational fit depends mainly on disciplinary and teaching skills and ethics adherence.

Which Holland interest type is more suitable for this occupation? The O*NET interest code is SI: Social (teaching and advising and collaborating with students and peers) and Investigative (investigating disciplinary questions with research and evidence and data); it can be used to explore task preferences, not to predict performance.
This page does not provide validation research on how personality or interests affect performance in this occupation, and no individual work performance conclusions are drawn from questionnaires.

Can someone who is not good at math do this occupation? Basic data and statistics and research methods and result interpretation abilities are needed; a quantitative foundation can be filled in through training and tool support, but a complete inability to adapt to data and research would be clearly limiting (especially in research positions).

Does this occupation require high emotional intelligence? It requires emotional stability and empathy and communication and management skills, but no specific assessment scores. Classroom and student and peer communication and semester pressure require self-regulation and communicating and reporting according to procedure.

Can the Enneagram be used to judge whether I am suited? No. The Enneagram is a self-exploration tool and does not constitute a conclusion about occupational ability or fit; judging fit should look at whether you can complete course design and teaching and assessment work under academic integrity and ethics and authorization requirements.

The editors recommend using approved simulated materials to complete a course and assessment note, recording feedback and capabilities still to be added; this is an exploration recommendation and does not prove greater predictive accuracy than a questionnaire. Real student data and teaching are handled according to authorization.

Fit signals: willing to be responsible for teaching quality and the safety of students and patients within academic integrity and ethics and institutional authorization, able to switch between lesson preparation and teaching and assessment and advising and research while maintaining attention to the basis and records, and able to uphold evidence and integrity and review under semester and academic pressure and to report and hand over according to policy in the event of academic or safety issues or exceeding authority.

Caution signals: finding it hard to teach and communicate with students and peers over the long term, or hard to bear responsibility for teaching quality and the safety of students, colleagues, and patients and the consequences of errors, or unwilling to take responsibility for the truthfulness of academic integrity and data and privacy compliance, or unwilling to report and hand over according to policy when authorization is exceeded.

entries.answer: The Health Specialties Teachers, Postsecondary on this page is the exact occupation O*NET 25-1071.00 (Health Specialties Teachers, Postsecondary): teach courses in health specialties, covering fields such as dentistry, laboratory technology, medicine, pharmacy, public health, therapy, and veterinary medicine. Core tasks include preparing course materials (importance 84), following developments in the field by reading literature and talking with colleagues and attending conferences (83), evaluating and grading student assignments and papers (81), supervising laboratory sessions (80), compiling and administering and grading examinations (79), maintaining student attendance and grade records (79), initiating and facilitating and moderating classroom discussions (78), preparing and delivering topics such as public health and stress management and workplace health promotion for undergraduate or graduate students (79), planning and evaluating and revising curricula (75), supervising teaching and internships and research (74), participating in admissions and registration and job placement (72), and conducting research and publishing and applying for funding (64 and 69). Common job titles include Assistant Professor and Associate Professor and Clinical Professor and Instructor and Lecturer and Occupational Therapy Professor and Pharmacology Professor and Physical Therapy Professor and Professor and Public Health Professor; on the 25-1071.00 page, O*NET shows that the main industry for this occupation in the United States is educational services. What is described on this page is the U.S. occupational classification scope, and wages and employment follow this occupation's (25-1071.00) own scope (annual wage only); the content on this page does not constitute any medical, diagnostic, treatment, medication, legal, or education policy advice.
entries.question: What exactly does this occupation do?

entries.answer: The core differences lie in subject matter, output, and authorization level: this occupation takes health specialties course teaching and student advising and teaching research and research as its subject matter, and its output is courses and teaching materials and assessment and grading and advising and teaching research and research findings records; Postsecondary Nursing Instructors and Teachers (25-1072.00) take nursing course teaching and clinical mentoring as their subject matter; Health Education Specialists (21-1091.00) take population health education and promotion programs as their subject matter; Clinical Nurse Specialists (29-1141.04) take clinical nursing and diagnosis and treatment as their subject matter; Postsecondary Biological Science Teachers (25-1042.00) take biological science course teaching as their subject matter; Career and Technical Education Teachers (25-1194.00) take career and technical course teaching as their subject matter; Education Teachers (25-1081.00) take education course teaching as their subject matter; and Postsecondary Psychology Teachers (25-1066.00) and Postsecondary Social Work Teachers (25-1113.00) take psychology and social work course teaching respectively as their subject matter. Subject matter and work and authorization level all differ, and the authority for clinical diagnosis and treatment and medical advice and grades and academic sanctions and disclosure cannot be carried over across positions.

For this occupation in 2025, the median annual wage is $107,310; the 10th percentile annual wage is $59,270, the 25th percentile $75,690, the 75th percentile $210,370, and the 90th percentile $322,020 (BLS OEWS 2025, as presented by O*NET). Employment and growth: 2024 employment 289,600, projected growth for 2024—2034 of 7% or higher (much faster than average, marked Bright Outlook), with about 27,400 average annual openings during the period (including growth and replacements). The above excludes benefits and bonuses, does not apply to other jurisdictions, and does not represent adjacent occupations; the openings consist mainly of replacement needs, and demand is affected by the structure of higher education enrollment and institutional funding and clinical teaching demand.

entries.answer: There is no national occupational wage distribution precisely corresponding to this U.S. occupation. Mainland China has similar positions in the fields of higher medical education and nursing education and applied health specialties teaching and continuing medical education, and their work and qualifications and standards and records are governed by the Education Law of the People's Republic of China, the Higher Education Law of the People's Republic of China, the Teachers Law of the People's Republic of China, the Academic Degrees Law of the People's Republic of China, and the Basic Medical and Health Promotion Law of the People's Republic of China, as well as the code of professional conduct for higher education teachers and regulations on clinical teaching and research ethics and personal information protection (higher education teaching and clinical teaching must follow standards and specifications; matters involving diagnosis, treatment, and medication must be carried out by institutions and personnel with the corresponding qualifications; and students' and patients' and participants' personal information must be protected in accordance with the law and handled under the minimum necessary principle), but public occupational statistics do not list this occupation separately: the National Bureau of Statistics publishes average wages of urban unit employees by industry category, which is an industry scope that does not distinguish occupations. Under the evidence policy of this page, the China section only registers the statistical scope and the visible "Evidence insufficient:" marker and does not use industry averages, job posting offers, or U.S. data for cross-jurisdiction extrapolation of starting salaries, medians, or personal income. entries.answer: In this occupation, course materials and handouts and item bank drafts and literature and data and grade and attendance ledger steps can already be assisted by generative and teaching and statistics tools, with moderate automation exposure; the direct impact of generative AI itself is concentrated in material and item bank drafts and document and data organization. The O*NET hot technologies page lists 9 software skills (Microsoft Office software 4%, Microsoft PowerPoint 2%, Microsoft Excel 2%, Microsoft Outlook 1%, Microsoft Word under 1%, Microsoft Access under 1%, etc.). Course design judgments and teaching and assessment and grading judgments, academic integrity and teaching and research ethics judgments, student advising and office hours, and teaching research and research judgments and responsibility remain with personnel who have the corresponding qualifications and authorization; O*NET shows a projected growth of 7% or higher for this occupation in 2024—2034 with a Bright Outlook marker, but projections are not equal to individual job outcomes.

entries.answer: Common failures include: improper course design or assessment or grading, or improper handling of coursework and academic integrity, or out-of-bounds provision of clinical and medication judgments; improper handling of student or patient or participant personal information and research data, missing informed consent or ethics review, or out-of-bounds sharing; distorted or version-uncontrolled grade or attendance or course or assessment or teaching research or funding records, or improper handling of academic integrity and conflicts of interest; making grade and academic sanction or clinical advice or external disclosure decisions beyond authorization; critical qualification or disciplinary or research or clinical mentoring capability resting on a single point; and insufficient adaptation of courses and assessment or accessibility and language and culture, or insufficient safety protection for students, colleagues, and patients. The control points are to verify and review and document according to program objectives and professional and industry standards and academic integrity and teaching and research ethics and privacy requirements, and to pause and report immediately when academic or academic integrity problems or safety or privacy or ethics risks or matters exceeding authorization arise. subject.name: Health Specialties Teachers, Postsecondary
subject.summary: The Health Specialties Teachers, Postsecondary corresponds to the exact occupation O*NET/SOC 25-1071.00 "Health Specialties Teachers, Postsecondary": teach courses in health specialties, covering fields such as dentistry, laboratory technology, medicine, pharmacy, public health, therapy, and veterinary medicine; core tasks include preparing course materials and teaching courses and leading discussions and supervising laboratories, evaluating and grading assignments and papers and compiling and administering and grading examinations, maintaining student attendance and grade records, supervising teaching and internships and research and holding office hours, conducting research and publishing and applying for funding, and participating in admissions and committees and academic service; common job titles include Assistant Professor and Associate Professor and Clinical Professor and Instructor and Lecturer and Professor and Public Health Professor. Official scope text: Teach courses in health specialties, in fields such as dentistry, laboratory technology, medicine, pharmacy, public health, therapy, and veterinary medicine. Scope note: the U.S. wage and employment and industry data presented by O*NET on the 25-1071.00 page are not marked as taken from a parent occupation, so this page labels them faithfully according to this occupation's own scope (25-1071.00); the wages on that page show only the annual wage distribution and not the hourly wage, and this page does not fill in an hourly wage; this occupation is projected to grow 7% or higher over 2024—2034 and is marked Bright Outlook, and O*NET places it in Job Zone Five (extensive preparation needed, SVP 8.0 and above). The content on this page does not constitute medical, diagnostic, treatment, medication, legal, or education policy advice.
